meta.title: OrionOS: a desktop that is alive
meta.description: OrionOS is a Linux system whose whole desktop is Orion: a living black hole, calm glass windows, one Orion button, coding agents you can watch, and your phone's fingerprint for every big decision.

hero.eyebrow: A Linux OS · free and open source
hero.title: Your desktop is alive.
hero.lede: OrionOS is Ubuntu with Orion as the whole desktop: a living black hole at the centre, calm glass windows, one Orion button, and helpers that do the work while you stay in charge.
hero.note: The preview runs in your browser with sample data. Nothing leaves your computer.

features.title: The living black hole
features.text: Orion's core sits in the middle of your desktop. It is calm when all is well, brighter while you talk, warmer when it is time to rest. Messages fall in as small comets; things waiting for your OK orbit it.

features.title: Start a project with Claude
features.text: Name it, pick a starter (web game, website, Python tool), say what you want, and watch it being built. Play it when it's ready.

features.title: Mission Control
features.text: Every agent job on one board: Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI, each in its own branch, with its live log, changes and cost. A second agent reviews the work. Nothing is merged until you approve it.

features.title: Your phone, paired in one go
features.text: Point your phone's camera at the QR code and check five words match. Then your phone shows what needs you, mirrors your inbox if you want, and approves big decisions with your fingerprint.

features.title: Privacy you can see
features.text: One dashboard lists everything Orion can see or hear, with one tap to turn each off. The camera and the hot mic are off until you turn them on, work on this computer, and always show a light.

features.title: Start Here and the Test Center
features.text: Double-click Start Here on Windows and it walks you through everything. The Test Center checks each part, one card at a time, with a big Do it for me button.

features.title: Glass windows, one Orion button
features.text: Gunmetal glass windows with a cobalt glow on the one in focus. One round Orion button opens a full-screen console: chat in the middle, every feature grouped around it. Type to find anything, and drag the button wherever you like.

features.title: Every chat in one place
features.text: Telegram, Discord, Messenger and your phone's messages in one inbox. Orion drafts replies in your style; nothing is ever sent until you tap Send.

features.title: Talk to it
features.text: Say "Orion, ..." and it listens. Speech is turned into text on this computer. The hot mic and the wake word are off until you turn them on, and Ctrl+Alt+M mutes it.

features.title: Skills it learns by watching
features.text: Say "Orion, watch what I do next", do a task once, and it becomes a skill you can run again by voice. Risky steps always ask first.

features.title: Guide Mode
features.text: Ask "show me how to connect to Wi-Fi" and Orion puts a ring around each button in turn. It only looks at the screen while a guide runs.

features.title: It can improve itself, with your OK
features.text: Ask for a change to Orion itself and you see a ghost preview first. Approve it and it swaps in; say "undo that" to put it back. The protected core can never change itself.

safety.title: Nothing sends without you
safety.text: Every message, post and reply waits for your tap. Voice and gestures never approve money or big decisions.

safety.title: Fingerprint for the big things
safety.text: Merges, payments and anything public need your fingerprint on your paired phone.

safety.title: Stays on your computer
safety.text: Screen reading, voice and the camera run on this computer. Orion sends no usage data anywhere.

safety.title: One tap to freeze
safety.text: The snowflake stops every agent, update and self-change at once. Only your phone can unfreeze it.

try.title: In a virtual machine
try.what: Nothing changes on your PC: OrionOS runs in a window on Windows.

try.title: From a USB stick
try.what: Start the PC from the stick. Your stuff lives encrypted on the stick.

try.title: Alongside Windows
try.what: Adds OrionOS next to Windows; pick one every time you start.

start_here.title: Not sure where to start?
start_here.text: Download the repository, open the folder on Windows and double-click Start Here.cmd. It checks your PC (changing nothing), sets Orion up and opens the Test Center.
start_here.honest: So far OrionOS has been tested in virtual machines, not yet on a real laptop. Keep Windows on any computer you depend on.
